Sentence (English): I bought my large capacity Whirlpool dishwasher a month ago.
Comments (English): [ Great Purchase ] || ---------------- || I bought my large capacity Whirlpool dishwasher a month ago. Love the quietness when it is operating. The third rack at the top is great for long utensils. I usually use the quick wash which works great even for a full load.I do find the middle rack is a challenge for placement of bowls so that they don't fall forward onto each other. Only issue I wonder about is the moisture on the inside door even though I use the dry choice. So far it has exceeded my expectations. Like any diswasher it is an indispensable asset in a kitchen. I highly recommend to anyone in search of a top-tier dishwashing experience.

Sentence (English): My previous home had a built-in dishwasher, but I wasn't satisfied with its cleaning power and it was too big, so I rarely used it.
Comments (English): [ It's comfortable. ] || ---------------- || My previous home had a built-in dishwasher, but I wasn't satisfied with its cleaning power and it was too big, so I rarely used it. That is why I didn't install one when I renovated my house this time. However, lately I've been suffering from trigger finger and elbow pain, making dishwashing difficult. While searching for a dishwasher, I found a product I had been eyeing on Coupang being sold at a very low price, so I ordered it right away. I even got a card discount, but when I checked now, it's being sold at a higher price (yay^^). Although it is a small size, it is suitable for washing dishes after a basic meal for a family of three. The cleaning power is good, and I really like that the door opens automatically when it finishes. It doesn't have a hot air drying function; it dries to about 70-80%, and if you leave the door open, it seems to gradually turn into a dryer. My kitchen isn't particularly small, so it feels a bit cramped having it on the ceiling, but I'm sure I'll get used to it^^. I hope to make good use of this product. I ran the drying mode in the evening, and when I checked the next morning, even the inside of the dishwasher was completely dry^^.

Sentence (English): This is a wonderful dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Best Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || This is a wonderful dishwasher. Quiet and cleans every layer very well. It does exactly what you expect when purchasing. The only issue from being perfect is the drying. It does not adequately dry and leaves the most of the upper dishes pretty wet even when using the sanitizing feature. I used the prerinse, preclean, less dishes, ect and it never quite helps. Opening the door and waiting for a few hours will achieve a good dryness (your third deck will most likely remain wet if you don't pull that out to dry) . You will get water spots as a result of the drying. To be frank; it's worth it because everything comes out clean. I've done plastic, bottles, glass, ceramic, and they all come out clean and no damage. Installation is very easy the slanted dish placement has a learning curve but it works well. Overal, I'd buy again because I'm fine with waiting on the drying.

Sentence (English): Purchased dishwasher for some of the features listed on website.
Comments (English): [ Overly complicated ] || ---------------- || Purchased dishwasher for some of the features listed on website. Turns out you can only access about half the features without connecting the dishwasher to the internet. The problems with THAT are many fold. First, the instructions are overly complex. Second, the webapp use really sucks eggs. Badly designed and not as user friendly as it should be. So to get the thing to work, I now have to have another crappy app living on my smartphone. And what happens if certain events related to my home network change (for example, I am required by my ISP to upgrade my router? ). Now I get the unmitigated joy of trying to reestablish my access to my appliance? And never mind if I sell my home. what then? Then there is the additional problem, that Bosch hasn't really ADDED features that are only available on line. Nope. They took features that you would normally expect of ANY dishwasher, and RESTRICTED them to oline only. This sort of anti customer behavior sucks. Frankly, after this experience, not at all inclined to consider Bosch products again.

The new dishwasher is fine and much quieter than the old one, but it does have some features that take some getting used to. The silverware basket has compartments that are almost too large and to retrieve the clean utensils you almost always have to touch the surface from which people will be eating. The older machine had a basket with a catch/release on the front--you could lay the tray down, unsnap the catch, fold it open, and grasp the silverware by the handle without touching the eating surface. The top basket is almost too customized for glassware. It is noted on the instructions that cereal/soup bowls can be placed down the center--but they stick out far enough to disallow the average glassware on the next row. Smaller items or mixing spoons, etc. will fit in that channel but not the full-sized drinking glass. The outer two rows on the top are nicely designed for cups and glasses with the exception of the two areas the house the tray adjustment brackets--the bracket sticks out far enough that the area will not hold a full-sized cup, glass, or wine glass. As I stated, some of this is just adjusting to a newer piece of equipment--this will happen over time and with experimentation I'm certain. On the plus side, the washer is very quiet at 57 decibels, cleans well with a nice selection of programming options and fits sleekly in the kitchen.

I miss the way our old dishwasher could be quietly closed early in the morning. But the unit does a great job at cleaning our dishes. It alerts us when we should clean the filter. When we should refil the rinse-aid, and we can connect to the bosch API to get cylce information into my home automation setup. I appreciate that there's also a no-cloud mode that I can turn on in that app. That way if the cloud service goes away someday, I can still use my dishwasher.I really wish that instead of a solid light on the front, that it was more of a progress bar or a countdown bar to quickly glance and see how long until the load is finished without opening an app. The third track is perfect. We don't use the utensil basket anymore. Great dishwasher. It has some quirks. But I think we'd get that with anyone today.

Comments (English): [ LG Repair Service, always a disappointment. ] || ---------------- || We bought our LG dishwasher in October of 2018. It is very quiet, (more about THAT later). It has done a good job overall on washing dishes but we've had to schedule repairs for a couple of issues. We purchased an extended warranty and thank goodness we did. For one visit the rubber piece that forms the seal for the water spray to reach the top rack was originally not installed properly and was replaced under warranty. As of now, the power supply fried and needed replacement. The first time the technician brought the wrong part because of an engineering change and had to re-order the correct part. So we waited for that. Just yesterday he replaced to power supply and left. When I went to run a load of dishes the machine gave out a loud 60 cycle noise when a motor would kick in and the washing cycle didn't kick in. I also noticed dirty rust colored water after the tech left so I ran a refresh cycle first which seemed to work OK oddly enough. I texted the technician yesterday and as of today he has not responded. I had to start all over requesting ANOTHER service call through the 800 LG service number. Now I have to wait 3 days for the technician to make it back out. I'm very frustrated with LG customer service. We had similar issues with our LG refrigerator which the tech was unable to fix. We now have a Frigidaire. No more LG products for us.

Sentence (English): I have had this dishwasher for about 2 years.
Comments (English): [ Lots of Cleaning Options ] || ---------------- || I have had this dishwasher for about 2 years. This has been a good dishwasher. I like almost everything. I like the third top shelf for large utensils and such. It functions well and has lots of cleaning options like temp boost. I really like that the controls are not visible and can not accidentally be pushed during the cycle. It is quiet enough for us to still hear tv. It has a light that lets you know the dishes are clean. There are two things that need improved. As much as my LG was a piece of junk, it had a well organized bottom rack. This GE needs to add an extra foldable middle row to make loading easier and more efficient with smaller items like bowls. Also the silverware holder could have slightly smaller holes. I do not like the organizer flap to place one piece of silverware in, I have a large family and we dirty a lot of dishes, so I just put them all in the basket. A lot of the spoon handles will slide through the hole and if you turn them upside down they don't always get as clean. Other than those two suggestions this is a 4.5 star dishwasher. This would be 5 star otherwise.

Sentence (English): We purchased this 800 series dishwasher (along with the 800 series refrigerator) due to our previous experience with a Bosch dishwasher several years ago.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and Clean ] || ---------------- || We purchased this 800 series dishwasher (along with the 800 series refrigerator) due to our previous experience with a Bosch dishwasher several years ago. When our '90s dishwasher died, we decided to research new machines and buy something that would last, despite being well ahead of our total kitchen remodel. Overall, the dishwasher is excellent and we're happy they still have the red LED light on the floor to indicate when it is running as it is so quiet. There is a bit of a learning curve, and per the instructions we are using pods instead of liquid detergent and also researched our local moderately hard water levels in order to calibrate the appropriate salt additive. While the unit is the same size as the previous unit, it does seem to have less capacity. As such, we now use the top 3rd row for silverware and have removed the actual basket to allow more plates on the lower level. It does sound like overkill, but we are seriously considering having two dishwashers in our future kitchen island to keep up while entertaining; I previously thought this was ridiculous but I may be a convert! Install was certainly more intense than less sophisticated machines, and the instructions were probably 95% correct, but there were missing screws for the 3rd and final kickplate. There was not "strap" on the back for cord routing, there was no removal of the rubber skirt and, therefore, no need to reattach as the instructions noted and illustrated. I imagine this was due to a single manual applying to a few different models. Bosch did send a miscellaneous packet of screws which appears to include the 13mm screws with plastic caps, but I've not spent the time to correct the temporary screws that I purchased at a hardware store. Other than a few occassional odd sounds and a few failed starts (powered down and restarted without issue just like your iphone or laptop; temporary glitch) I would definitely purchase again

Sentence (English): I finally bought the dishwasher I've been longing for.
Comments (English): I finally bought the dishwasher I've been longing for. It was a dishwasher I had been eyeing for a while, just keeping it in my shopping cart. To be honest, I was a bit skeptical; I heard things like you absolutely have to pre-wash the dishes and that it's a bit of a hassle. But I didn't bother with pre-washing; I just removed the food scraps and put everything straight into the dishwasher. Was it because the detergent was good? It cleaned up really well, leaving absolutely no grease, rice grains, or sauce behind. Also, if you put too many dishes in and run it with the bottom washing blades stuck to the rack, of course it won't clean properly. You need some space for it to clean well. If you scrub too hard, sauce might still get stuck. I didn't pre-wash; I just removed the food scraps and put everything straight into the dishwasher. As you can see in the picture, there isn't a single grain left, right? The tongs at the bottom were used to cook fish, so they had some hard fish residue on them, but they came off completely spotless. I am totally satisfied. I still don't pre-wash; I just run it as is. As soon as I finish eating, I put everything in the dishwasher and run it. I use the "Powerful" setting for heavy dirt, "Standard" for moderate dirt, and just the "Quick" setting for lighter items. Please do not complain about the inconvenience before using it; look up the information carefully and familiarize yourself with the instruction manual. It cleans better than washing by hand. There is nothing wrong with the machine. If it doesn't clean well, you can try adding a detergent additive. Of course, it won't clean properly if you fill it up too much just to save space. There is a high probability of sauce residue, so please keep the dishwasher's operating principle in mind when using it. Position the dishwasher so that the water streams reach the rotating blades well. If you run it, you will find sparkling, stain-free dishes! I used it after thoroughly reading the instruction manual beforehand. Since I have a water purifier cord, using the installed model is very convenient for me. However, if you do not block the water inlet for the non-installation type, it will leak. I accidentally threw away the cap and blocked it with just any cap. If you are installing it, make sure to block the water inlet for the non-installation type with a cap. There is a leak. Also, do not expect good drying performance from this. The drying isn't the best part. Ceramic items dry if I use rinse aid, but other dishes don't dry very well. Nevertheless, considering my intended purpose—dishwashing—it is excellent and I love it. I used to hate washing dishes, but I feel liberated now. I feel a sense of catharsis looking at the spotless dishes. Also, I cook frequently, and I used to feel tired from cleaning up and washing dishes afterwards, but thanks to the dishwasher, that fatigue has been significantly reduced. Furthermore, it really removes sauce residue from takeout dishes completely. Personally, I often cook large quantities of side dishes and fry food, so the burden has greatly diminished. I used to be extremely self-conscious about wiping off grease and washing dishes with dish soap multiple times, but that stress is gone now! Also, the controls are relatively intuitive, making it easy to operate. Regarding the noise, I think it is acceptable, but if you are sensitive to sound, you might find it loud. Sentence (English): I'm still getting used to remembering to empty the third rack, but it is convenient.
Comments (English): [ Flexible, holds a lot ] || ---------------- || I'm still getting used to remembering to empty the third rack, but it is convenient. Upon delivery, the lower rack was always falling off the track, it could never be right. I called LG and they sent a new one that is excellent; no problem at all. I like how flexible the racks are for adjusting tines to each load's needs but so far I have a few bowls that just never seem to find the right size width of tines to hold them in a way that they aren't laying down and taking up a lot of room. The options of placement are flexible enough for me to solve the problem by the time it's full enough to start. I like that I can wash half a load at a time, though I haven't done so yet. I simply haven't read the directions for any of the fancy functions like using the wifi and phone. My favorite thing about it is how quiet it is. It really is quiet, though it was more so before I cut the sound insulation sheet in attempts to allow the door to open all the way when I thought it prevented the rack from remaining on track. I cut it so the door would open further and now I have less sound insulation and nobody seems to be able to identify the fact that the insulation sheet exists to find a replacement. (LG knows what it is but says it's from the store and installers. The store doesn't know what it is and the installers won't respond. It was part of the dishwasher, not any plumbing part.) It would have helped immensely if the directions for it's installation were better. They were actually a hindrance. Look up the Youtube video for it's installation. Keywords LG sound insulation kit installation.

Sentence (English): The door of my existing built-in Samsung dishwasher broke.
Comments (English): [ Demolition must be done by the consumer. ] || ---------------- || The door of my existing built-in Samsung dishwasher broke. I called Samsung A/S, but they said they couldn't fix it, so I had no choice but to purchase a new one. Confirming and changing the delivery schedule via KakaoTalk notifications was incredibly convenient, as it was just a click or two away, eliminating the need to wait for the delivery person to call. However, the unexpected removal of the old dishwasher was a major problem. The first remodeling technician I visited told me I had to remove the old dishwasher myself (cut off the power and water supply) before installing the new one. This involved blocking the hot and cold water pipes coming from the rear wall, blocking the drain, and disconnecting the electrical wiring. I wasn't sure if I could handle this myself, so I decided to have Samsung help me with the installation. However, the delivery company and Samsung Service Center kept evading responsibility and repeatedly argued, delaying the installation for a week. I finally managed to purchase the parts myself at a hardware store and had the facility team at the management office complete the installation. However, the risk of water leakage made it a challenging process. Since my Samsung product was beyond repair, I had no choice but to replace it with another Samsung product. However, Samsung's stubborn stance was to only collect the old product and not to participate in the removal process, which was extremely disconcerting as a consumer. After some twists and turns, I finally got the product installed, but it was an inconvenient and difficult experience in many ways.
Comments (Original): [ 철거는 소비자가 직접해야함 ] || ---------------- || 기존에 빌트인된 삼성 식기세척기 도어가 고장났는데, 삼성 A/S를 불렀더니 못고친다하여 어쩔수 없이 신규구매를 진행했습니다. 카톡알림을 통한 배송일정 확정/변경은 일일이 배송기사의 전화를 기다릴 필요가 없이 클릭 한두번으로 처리되는점이  정말 편리했어요!반면 예상치도 못한 기존제품 철거가 큰 문제였습니다. 최초 방문한 리폼기사님께서 기존제품 철거작업을(단선, 단수 등) 소비자가 직접  선행해야 이후에 제품설치가 가능하다고 안내해주셨어요. 기존에 후면 벽으로부터 나온 온수, 냉수 수도관을 막아야하고 배수관도 막고, 전기선도 단선작업이 필요한 상황이었습니다. 이걸 소비자가 직접 하는게 가능한가 싶어서 삼성측에서 설치시 같이 작업해주는게 맞다고 생각했는데, 배송업체와 삼성서비스센터와의 책임 미루기 및 몇차례 실랑이로 일주일이나 제품설치가 미뤄졌어요. 결국 철물점에서 제가 부품들을 직접 사다가 관리사무소 시설팀 직원분께 부탁드려서 겨우 작업을 진행했는데, 누수 우려가 있는 작업이라 쉽지 않은 과정이었습니다. 사용중이던 삼성 제품이 수리가 불가하니 불가피하게 삼성->삼성 제품으로 교체를 한건데, 삼성에서는 기존 제품의 폐가전 수거만 해줄뿐 철거작업에는 절대로 개입하지 않으려는 완고한 태도였기에 소비자 입장에서 무척 당황스러웠습니다. 우여곡절 끝에 설치는 했는데 여러모로 불편하고 고생 많은 경험이었습니다.

I was actually thinking of removing the third tray to see if I like the set up better that way. To be honest, I prefer the dishwasher without the third pull out rack. Sentence (English): I'm pleased with the cleaning capabilities of this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Works as Expected ] || ---------------- || I'm pleased with the cleaning capabilities of this dishwasher. My dishes come out clean every time. I do wish there were options to buy portable dishwashers with more high quality features though. For example, the top of the silverware container should be on a hinge that you can easily lift and then drop back down as opposed to having to unclip both sides of it and then snap it back on (it becomes a two handed job, when it would have been so easy to make it a hinged top). I'm also not impressed that you literally have to take the top rack out of its tracks so that you can change its height. Again, a very simple feature that could have been improved. Other than that, there is no heated dry, but that's not GE's fault, rather the fault of government policy. That being said, my dishes are cleaned as hoped and I don't have to do any scrubbing myself (other than I always rinse off my dishes before putting them in the dishwasher). It is easy to operate, easy to roll around, and I really appreciate the sanitize feature. I wish the front and top did not show fingerprints so easily though. Even with that, I would not take the alternative: handwashing dishes.

Sentence (English): After a lengthy amount of research to replace our broken dishwasher, we decided on the Bosch 800 series.
Comments (English): [ Bosch 800 Series ] || ---------------- || After a lengthy amount of research to replace our broken dishwasher, we decided on the Bosch 800 series. We had compared this to Whirlpool, Samsung and even Thermador models. Having a bad experience with a Bosch years ago, we were hesitant. But based on other positive reviews we decided to go for it and paid the extra money for the 8oo series over the 500. In terms of function this is the best dishwasher we've ever owned. I would especially recommend this if you have children and/or use a lot of plastic dishware/tupperware. The dishwasher dries plastic completely every time (have to use a bit of rinse aid like JetDry but so worth it). No more unloading the dishwasher just to have them dry on the dishrack. This series does come with added features like Wifi connection. We upgraded simply for the better washing/drying capability. But these features are nice to have as well. Also the third rack on the top has been a lifesaver and the other two racks can fit quite a lot. I'm still giving this 5 stars, but a word of caution. We have a 100 year old house and our prior dishwasher was hardwired. This model does not come equipped with a hardwire capability (you have to buy an extra piece). Because of the tight space, we opted to have an electrician come in and add an outlet under the sink instead. If you already have this, setup will be easy. A learning curve for me as a homewoner, but double check what your current setup is so you can be prepared.

I hope my review helps many people make their own purchases. ^^ Honest product review. Purchased: Built-in 14-seater Samsung dishwasher. I worried a lot about whether I really needed a dishwasher, but I realized that worrying only delayed delivery and should have gotten it done sooner. I've used smaller ones several times, but they wouldn't fit my pots, so I had to wash the larger dishes by hand, which I never thought would be convenient. But now that it's built-in, it's so big that all my pots fit, and it's so convenient and great. I'm so happy that everything was taken care of in one go! I ordered the installation, and the technician for the foundation work contacted me the next day, and the installation was completed the day after. The day after the foundation work was completed, the technician for the dishwasher came the next day to install it! Since it requires foundation work and a built-in installation, it's difficult to complete the entire installation in one day, but it was nice to receive it promptly. The size was right for us, so we simply removed the drawer in that area and installed the dishwasher. If the size doesn't fit or the cabinets need to be reassembled, there's an additional charge. Ours fit perfectly without any additional charges. Installation was quick, and I was able to use it right away thanks to the detailed instructions provided after installation. It's a good idea to stock up on dishwasher detergent! It has a variety of functions, including rotating the top, and connecting your phone to it unlocks even more detailed features, making it a great choice. Overall: I like the ample interior space. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. I hope everyone has a delicious and happy meal and a relaxing time. I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it.
