Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. (흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. (흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

(흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

(흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. (흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. (흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. I hope everyone has a delicious and happy meal and a relaxing time. I hope my review was helpful.

(흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. I hope everyone has a delicious and happy meal and a relaxing time. I hope my review was helpful.

(흰 싱크대에 묘하게 톤 다른 글램화이트인데도 이쁨) -장점-모든 하단 설치 식기세척기의 허리다리 움직임 -단점-냄비, 큰 접시 다 수납 가능 -장점-가격이 저렴한 것도 필수인 가전제품도 아니니 충분히 고민해보세요.그리고, 맘 먹으셨다면 지르세요. 후회하지 않으실거예요. 모두가 맛있고 행복한 식사시간과 여유로운 휴식시간을 가지시길 바래요. 제 후기가 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다~

Comments (English): [ A very, very detailed review from a first-time dishwasher user. ] || ---------------- || (Who needs a dishwasher?) The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1. An LG model that's slightly cheaper than this one. LG is priced higher than Samsung, so this one lacks the top spoon section. It didn't significantly impact my purchase, but I excluded the Samsung model because it's easier to use the app. 2. A Samsung model that was slightly cheaper than my current model. - Emphasis - The app doesn't work. There's no LCD on the front, so I can't tell how many hours are left. Honestly, I was just tempted to buy this one. (Be careful before buying, and if you did, what should I do?). 1. - Emphasis - It's absolutely essential to compare prices extensively. I spent a month considering it, and it was less than 80% full. 2. Please set a schedule based on whether the remodeling is easy. I installed it where the built-in kimchi refrigerator was removed. Since there was a little extra length, I just cut the mop holder. They came, removed the kimchi refrigerator, cut the mop holder, and that was it. (It took 30 minutes? -2 hours once the renovation starts). -Caution- The installation team took care of the removal. 3. Installation actually took longer. I had used up half a day off, but two incredibly skilled installers came and got it done in no time. That's why I chose a major company. Both the renovation and installation engineers were very friendly. 4. Please clear the area to be renovated beforehand on the renovation day, and clear the cabinets under the sink before the installation day. 5. -Emphasis- Go buy detergent. If you bought a machine, you have to use it. The installer gave us one as a service, but there's no guarantee. They offer discount coupons, but you want to try it right away. (So, what are the features?) 1. Use the app. When I looked up the information, I only confirmed that it supports SmartThings. The functionality was a bit disappointing. It can be operated whether the power is on or off. To operate it, you have to go to the machine, press the smart control, and close the door. It's a one-time operation. Of course, I have to go to the dishwasher anyway to add detergent, so I'll press start while I'm at it. Instead, I can check the remaining time without having to go all the way to the machine. - A huge plus - You can pause it midway. Additional cycles are available (for individual drying cycles or for plastic, glass cups, etc.). 2. Hot air drying. Of course, it helps, but it's not dramatic. - Some say - it increases the electricity bill quite a bit. And - a huge minus - you can see water stains. I could see them in the natural air cycle, but you bought a dishwasher, so you expect things to go up, right? It's not that bad. - Emphasis - Of course, not all dishes show water stains. I run it before work, turn off the hot air dryer -> After work, they're dry, but I find water stains on the Glass Lock. Next time, I run it with the hot air dryer -> It's a little better, but I also find water stains. I use a discount coupon to buy rinse aid (emphasis - this is so inconvenient! You spill the rinse aid container when you put it in) and run it -> Same thing. I'm thinking it's a water problem in my area. Don't expect it to be too flashy. 3. Recommended mode. Night mode. I originally left it on, but I forgot about the smart control, so I turned it on after working overtime, and it was really quiet. Of course, it runs more slowly, so if the contamination level is high, run it hard during the day. There are various modes for sterilizing glass cups, plastic, and baby bottles, but it's better than nothing. Night mode and top speed also work very well. 4. The dishes are constantly being washed. I don't do a pre-wash - I strongly emphasize this - but organizing is essential. Of course, I remove food. I always soak edible items for a certain amount of time and rinse them before putting them in. - Strongly emphasize this - Especially for chili oil, always stir anything to remove most of the color before putting them in. If the filter part below gets dirty, it's the end. (Photo attached) I didn't want to know either. I put a pot in it, but not a frying pan. I wash the rice cooker separately, of course. Sometimes, I mess up Tetris and have to dry the water that's pooled in there, so I don't even bother putting the dryer away. (Conclusion: So what do you think?) I'm—and I emphasize—very satisfied. When I eat, I take out all the dishes. I feel like I'm being treated well. I leave the dishwasher running, and every time I go to wash it, I feel like I'm spending my own money and saving time. (Conclusion). Using the app. Freestanding (+easy and pretty construction with a cut-out mop holder). Hot air drying. Standalone drying. - Pros-. Higher price compared to other models, but not sure if it's worth the price compared to the above performance. - Cons-. The exterior is pretty. (It's a glam white with a strangely different tone from the white sink, but it's still pretty.) - Pros-. The lower leg movement of all bottom-mounted dishwashers. - Cons-. Can hold pots and large plates. - Pros-. It's not cheap, nor is it a must-have appliance, so think carefully. And if you're determined, buy it. You won't regret it. I hope everyone has a delicious and happy meal and a relaxing time. I hope my review was helpful.

The first thing you're thinking about is the amount of dishes, but you probably didn't worry about it until now, right? -Emphasis- Even if you're cooking alone, dishes are still a chore. The biggest considerations when purchasing a dishwasher, aside from the price, are: 1. Whether you cook at home. If you don't use the dishwasher, cleaning becomes a hassle and it becomes a burden. 2. The number of dishes you have. If you don't have any, you'll probably be loading two 12-person dishes every time, so count them first. (If you're buying a 12-person dishwasher, where will you place it?) Be sure to measure the length of a suitable spot near the sink before deciding. People often place it directly underneath, but even if it's not, a nearby spot is definitely more convenient. If it's too close, moving dishes will be inconvenient, and the renovation time and cost will be a bonus. (What to Buy). Start with a small one, especially if you have a small family. Except for those with less than six people. -Emphasis- An automatic door and pot storage are essential. Countertops take up more sink space than you might think. Storage is limited if you use a large bowl. It's not cheap either. -> I changed it to a 12-person model. I searched Coupang and found exactly three options. 1.
